segments.expected: Cold. Grit. The weave of the canvas. There was a great deal in a good hand, and she listened through all of it, and could not find a push.
segments.transcript: Cold, grit, the weave of the canvas. There was a great deal in a good hand, and she listened through all of it, and could not find a push.

segments.expected: So it was one or the other. It was a needle with no scale, saying that something under a hundredweight of waxed cloth was keeping time. Or it was a frightened girl reading her own blood. She had the method for telling which. It wanted a second person and a word spoken aloud, and she had her tongue held by a card with four signatures on it.
segments.transcript: So it was one or the other. It was a needle with no scale, saying that something under a hundredweight of waxed cloth was keeping time. Or it was a frightened girl reading her own blood. She had the method for telling which. It wanted a second person and a word spoken aloud. And she had her tongue held by a card with four signatures on it.

segments.expected: She had seen that. She had sat on a mangle bench with a ticket on her knee and written it down. Takes it by its two corners, arms wide. Folds from the far edge. Always has the last of it.
segments.transcript: She had seen that. She had sat on a mangle bench with a ticket on her knee and written it down. Takes it by its two corners, arms wide, folds from the far edge, always has the last of it.

segments.expected: And under it, in a cross woman's own words: You never fold with a thing lying on the far side. It all comes to you.
segments.transcript: and under it in a cross woman's own words. You never fold with a thing lying on the far side. It all comes to you.

segments.expected: It was not a hem. It was a sheet, and it was being folded, and there were sixty drams of open ash lying in the middle of it.
segments.transcript: It was not a hem, it was a sheet, and it was being folded, and there were sixty drams of open ash lying in the middle of it.

segments.expected: It came over the heap, and over the canvas, and it was laid on the near edge corner to corner, exactly as a laundress lays one. There was no gap in it anywhere. There was a white fold a pace high, with a cloth inside it, and sixty drams of ash inside the cloth, and at the top of it a man's two arms going in to the wrist.
segments.transcript: It came over the heap and over the canvas, and it was laid on the near edge corner to corner, exactly as a laundress lays one. There was no gap in it anywhere. There was a white fold, a pace high, with a cloth inside it, and sixty drams of ash inside the cloth, and at the top of it a man's two arms going into the wrist.

segments.expected: "I've not said a word," said Stroud.
The card came at ten on Friday night, and it was the same three words.
segments.transcript: The card came at 10 on Friday night, and it was the same three words.

segments.expected: "What's that at its heels?" said Rhea.
segments.transcript: What's that at its heels? said Rhea.

segments.expected: "I'll read it, then." Rhea tilted the slate to the van's lamp. "Before. A string of four, on end, at the coal wharf below the Hythe. Its tear's at the river stair. A hem lying at its foot, three paces by two, which the book calls ground. Nothing lit inside sixty paces but my gate; the Hythe's dark, on the warden's word. Asked of anybody beyond their card: nothing. The second kneels at the catcher's left hem and holds her tongue until the bag is sealed." She lowered it. "What's there? Mace."
segments.transcript: I'll read it then. Rhea tilted the slate to the van's lamp. Before. A string of four on end at the coal wharf below the hythe. Its tears at the river stair. segments.expected: "I don't like it," she said. "I've no reason. I've only a dislike, and I've stood a good many floors on a dislike and been wrong." She hung the slate on her belt. "Top rung, on the catcher's word. Go."
segments.transcript: I don't like it, she said. I've no reason, I've only a dislike, and I've stood a good many flaws on a dislike and been wrong. She hung the slate on her belt. Top rung, on the catcher's word. Go.

segments.expected: Six in seven, said Anwen's ink, in a laundry order book. Of five wrong calls, four were at a pulse over ninety.
